_comment: THE single source of truth for the question critic. Both the Python module
and the shipped single-file web tool read this, and CI fails if the HTML's
embedded copy has fallen out of step.
It is a data file rather than code in each language because the same rules
in two hand-written implementations drift, quietly, and you find out when
the two tools disagree in front of a founder. The runner in this repo
already carries that hazard with its embedded SCRIPTS block; no reason to
regex          fires when the pattern matches
regex_absent   fires when the pattern does NOT match
multi_sentence fires when the text holds more than one sentence-ending ?

rules.name: hypothetical
rules.pattern: \b(would you|would your|could you see yourself|do you think you('d| would)|if (?:you|we|there) (?:were|was|had|could)|imagine if|hypothetically|in future would|will you ever)\b
rules.why: People are cheerfully, sincerely wrong about their own future behaviour. A yes here costs them nothing and tells you nothing.
rules.suggestion: Ask what they did instead: “When did you last hit that problem, and what did you do?”

rules.name: pitching
rules.pattern: \b(our (?:product|app|platform|tool|solution|software)|we(?:'re| are) building|we(?:'ve| have) built|my (?:product|app|startup|idea)|what do you think of (?:this|our|my)|does this sound|would this be useful|how much would you pay for (?:this|it|our))\b
rules.why: The moment they know what you want to hear, you stop getting data and start getting politeness. You cannot un-ring that bell for the rest of the interview.
rules.suggestion: Describe nothing. Ask how they handle the problem today and what it costs them.

rules.name: leading
rules.pattern: \b(don't you (?:think|agree|find)|wouldn't you|isn't it (?:true|frustrating|annoying)|surely|obviously|as you know|i(?:'m| am) sure you|how (?:frustrating|annoying|painful) is)\b
rules.why: You have supplied the answer inside the question. Whatever comes back is yours, not theirs.
rules.suggestion: Strip the judgement out and let them supply it, or not.

rules.name: scale
rules.why: A 7 out of 10 is not a finding. It compresses the one thing you came for, which is the reason behind the number.
rules.suggestion: Ask for the reason directly, and the last occasion it applied.

rules.name: closed
rules.message: Opens with a word that invites yes or no
rules.why: Closed questions get closed answers, and a one-word answer is a dead end you then have to dig out of.
rules.suggestion: Start with what, how, when or “walk me through”.

rules.name: double-barrelled
rules.message: Two asks joined in one sentence
rules.why: They answer whichever half is easier and you will not notice the other went missing.
rules.suggestion: Split them. The runner shows one item per screen for exactly this reason.

rules.name: jargon
rules.why: It either means nothing to them or signals that you are selling. Both cost you candour.
rules.suggestion: Say it the way they would say it to a colleague.

rules.name: absolute
rules.why: Invites a correction rather than an account, and people argue with the word instead of answering.
rules.suggestion: Ask about a specific recent instance instead.

rules.name: multi-part
rules.message: More than one sentence in a single item
rules.why: Fine if the later ones are follow-up probes you ask after the first is answered. A problem only if they are separate topics competing for one answer.
rules.suggestion: If they are separate topics, split them into their own items.

rules.name: long
rules.why: By the end they are answering the last clause and have forgotten the first.
rules.suggestion: Cut it to the one thing you actually want to know.

rules.name: no-past-anchor
rules.pattern: \b(last time|walk me through|tell me about (?:a|the) time|what happened|how do you currently|how did you|when did you last|what did you|show me|the last (?:time|one|job|week|month))\b
rules.message: Not anchored to something that actually happened
rules.why: Questions grounded in a real past event get specifics; ungrounded ones get opinions, and opinions are the cheapest thing a person can give you.
rules.suggestion: Consider anchoring it: “the last time…”, “walk me through…”, “what happened when…”.

limits: These rules check HOW a question is asked, never WHETHER it is worth asking. A script can pass every rule and still probe nothing that matters.
